newsitem.title: UK: Copper slumps $70 on LME on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Copper slumps $70 on LME on long liquidation.

text.p: Copper prices were $70 lower by the end of Tuesday's morning trading session on the London Metal Exchange (LME), hit by nervous long liquidation and trade/producer selling, traders said.
Benchmark three months futures finished the morning at $1,946 a tonne, against $2,016 on Monday afternoon.
Copper slumps $70 on LME on long liquidation
The losses came despite a big fall in LME warehouse stocks, which fell 13,475 tonnes to a six-year low of 132,350 tonnes.

The market's failure to react to the stock figure suggested to some traders that long positiions originally belonging to Japan's Sumitomo Corp were still being sold into rallies. On Monday, the market hit a two-month high of $2,042.
"To me it's a miracle this market isn't any higher. Some positions must still be around from the Sumitomo scandal," a senior trader said.
The next downside objective is $1,900, dealers said.
